vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: ai-pa
Version: 1.0.0

The skill manages a directory of personal assistant contacts and uses a CLI tool called 'gog' to interact with Google Calendar and Gmail. It is classified as suspicious due to the use of python3 -c commands in SKILL.md that incorporate user-provided strings via direct substitution, creating a risk of Python/shell injection. Additionally, the skill handles sensitive PII (names, phones, emails) and relies on a non-standard utility for high-privilege communication tasks without explicit input sanitization.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions broadly match a PA-directory/calendar/email use case, but they omit required credentials and leave open-ended messaging/transport steps — these inconsistencies could lead to unexpected access or actions.

dimensions.detail: Name/description align with a PA coordination skill and the included pa-directory example is appropriate. However, the SKILL.md clearly expects use of an external CLI ('gog') and account credentials (GOG_ACCOUNT and gog auth) for calendar and email operations, yet the skill declares no required environment variables or primary credential. That mismatch is disproportionate and unexplained.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions read and write a local pa-directory.json (expected) and run Python one-liners (fine), but they also instruct sending messages to PAs, broadcasting to group JIDs, waiting for replies, and running 'gog' to send mail/create calendar events without specifying which messaging transport/tool will be used. This vagueness grants broad discretion to the agent (which endpoints/tools to use) and references agent memory logging. The agent could attempt to use arbitrary messaging APIs or modify auth state (gog auth add) — actions outside the explicit, declared scope.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no bundled code — lowest install risk. Nothing will be written to disk by an installer, though the skill's instructions do write to workspace files (pa-directory.json) at runtime.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md uses environment variables and auth flows (GOG_ACCOUNT, gog auth) and will need credentials for calendar/email and potentially messaging services, but the registry metadata lists no required env vars or primary credential. Requiring unaffiliated credentials (or not declaring required secrets) is a red flag: there's no explicit declaration of what tokens/keys the skill needs or which services it will access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and has no install-time persistence. Model invocation is allowed (platform default), so the agent could autonomously run the described commands. Combined with the vague messaging and undeclared credential requirements, that autonomy increases risk — consider limiting autonomous invocation until the credential/tooling questions are resolved.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill looks like a plausible PA coordination helper, but there are important inconsistencies you should resolve before installing: (1) The SKILL.md expects a 'gog' CLI and an environment variable (GOG_ACCOUNT) plus authentication commands (gog auth add) but the skill metadata declares no required credentials — ask the author which credentials/tokens are needed and why they aren't declared. (2) The instructions for messaging/broadcasting are vague about which messaging platform or API will be used (SMS, WhatsApp, internal chat, etc.); ask which transport the skill will call and what credentials/access it will need. (3) The skill will read and can overwrite data/pa-directory.json — review that file for sensitive owner contact info and consider running the skill in a sandboxed environment. (4) Because the agent could autonomously send emails/messages if allowed, consider disabling autonomous invocation or require explicit user confirmation for any outgoing communications. If you plan to use this, request explicit documentation of required env vars and the exact external tools/endpoints (and verify the 'gog' CLI's provenance) before granting access.
